title: 亲亲, 举高高, 想得挺美
subtitle: Texting with Scarlett, Nov 2026
kick: Conversation Practice · readable text first · audio optional
focus: 亲亲 · 吻 · 举高高 · 想得挺美 · 不急
key: synthetic audio is optional. This page is readable without clips. When a clip is added later, it is computer speech and the label says synthetic. Simplified characters are the main script on this page. Grey characters are traditional. ☰ Options flips the script and can hide pinyin or English. The pinyin line under the English is the dictionary reading with tone marks.
foot: Study cards. Personal names, contact details, and screenshots are not included. Audio is not required to publish the entry.

sections.title: Lines
sections.kick: Tone-mark pinyin, English, and a word breakdown on every line

items.note: The verb. 吻 is the noun for a kiss. In texts, 亲 is the usual casual choice.
A playful, baby-talk way to say kisses. Sweeter than 吻 in a text.
The noun. For a casual text, 亲 or 亲亲 often sounds more natural than 吻.

items.en: I want to give you eight kisses.
items.py: Wǒ xiǎng gěi nǐ bā ge wěn

items.en: I want to kiss you eight times.
items.py: Wǒ xiǎng qīn nǐ bā xià
items.note: 下 counts how many times an action happens.

items.en: You should be called 李佳吻 (a pun on 李佳雯).
items.note: Playful pun: 吻 wěn sounds almost like 雯 wén in her name 李佳雯. Not a real name change.

items.en: Oh, I see; so that's how it is.
Ah, so that's how it is.

items.py: A a a a yǒu dào lǐ
items.note: Repeating 啊 is natural and playful in casual texting, like a drawn-out "ahhh."

items.en: Can you give me six kisses?
items.py: Nǐ kě yǐ gěi wǒ liù ge wěn ma

items.en: Can you give me six kisses? (cutesy)
items.py: Nǐ kě yǐ gěi wǒ liù ge qīn qīn ma
items.note: Sweeter and more playful than the version with 吻.
下 counts the times. 嘛 (not 吗) adds a coaxing, pleading tone.

items.py: Gěi wǒ liù ge qīn qīn ma
items.note: 嘛 adds a coaxing tone, softer than a plain request with 吗.

items.en: You really like six, don't you?
items.py: Nǐ hěn xǐ huan liù shì bu shì
items.note: Teasing. 是不是 at the end is a tag question, like "right?"

items.py: Měi cì dōu shì liù ge

items.note: A set phrase. 六 sounds lucky here because of this saying, which is why "six is 顺" is a cheeky reply.
A playful reply to being teased about always picking six, nodding to 六六大顺.

items.py: Nà jīn tiān gěi wǒ qī ge ba
items.note: 吧 softens it into a suggestion.

items.en: I can give you six kisses.
items.py: Kě yǐ gěi nǐ liù ge wěn
items.note: A turn-down of seven that still offers six.

items.py: Hǎo ba liù ge yě hěn hǎo

items.note: The doubled form makes it cute, like a kid asking for a hug.
Baby-talk, like a kid asking to be picked up and lifted in the air. 高高 is doubled for cuteness.

items.en: Come here, hug, up you go!
items.py: Lái bào bào jǔ gāo gāo

items.note: A playful brush-off, literally "you're imagining it pretty beautifully," like "aren't you getting ahead of yourself."

words.en: links the verb to how it's done

items.py: Wǒ zài wài miàn zuò zhe ne
